DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City DILG OPINION No. 311 s.P2022 APR 25 2022 DIR. ALEX C. ROLDAN Regional Director, DILG Region Xl #58 McArthur Highway, Matina Davao City Dear Dir. Roldan. This pertains to your Memorandum dated 15 March 2022 requesting for an opinion on the proposed provincial ordinance adopting IPMR per Legislative District in the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of the Province of Davao Oriental. We concur to the position of the concerned Bureau that as of this writing, there is no specific law that would serve as legal basis for the proposed IP Mandatory Representative per legislative district. However, while no specific law mandates that IP Mandatory representation should be per legislative district, we submit that the constitutional and statutory bases of said representation suffice to support a per legislative district representation as necessity arises, Viz: Section IO, Article II, of the 1987 Philippine Constitution, provides that the State shall promote social justice in all phases of national development. Corollary to that, Section 17, Article XIV of the 1987 Philippine Constitution also provides that the State shall recognize, respect, and protect the rights of indigenous cultural communities to preserve and develop their cultures, traditions, and institutions. Section 16 of R.A. No. 8371, otherwise known as "The Indigenous Peoples' Rights Act of 1997", provides that the "ICCs/lPs have the right to participate fully, if they so choose, at all levels of decision-making in matters which may affect their rights, lives and destinies through procedures determined by them as well as to maintain and develop their own indigenous political structures. Consequently, the State shall ensure that the ICCs/lPs shall be given mandatory representation in policy making bodies and other local legislative councils." Considering the legislative intent embodied in the Constitution and the Indigenous Peoples' Rights Act which is gleaned towards protection of ICCs'/lPs' rights through proper representation in local legislative bodies, it can be deduced that in the existence of different Indigenous Cultural Communities and Indigenous Peoples in the territorial jurisdiction of different legislative districts, the representation in the provincial level may as well be per legislative district. This would ensure proportionate representation "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

as well as fairness and equality with the view that ICCs/lPs participation in the provincial legislative bodies on matters affecting their development shall not be limited to the legislative district thus represented. We likewise acknowledge the aspect pointed out by the concerned Regional Office that sectoral representation in the sanggunian is limited to three seats and only one of which is allocated to the representative from the indigenous cultural communities per Section 467 (b) of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Governmerit Code of 1991". However, it is noteworthy that R.A. No. 8371, otherwise known as "The Indigenous Peoples' Rights Act of 1997" which prescribed mandatory ICCs/IPs representation is a later law, enacted and became effective in 1997. In fact, Section 83 thereof provides that Presidential Decree No. 410, Executive Order Nos. 122-b and 122-c, and all other laws, decrees, order, rules and regulations or parts thereof inconsistent with said Act are repealed and modified accordingly. It is now incumbent for the DILG and NICP to incorporate in the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) an interpretation that is aligned to the intent of passing R.A. 8371. On this, we submit that said law is not passed merely to reiterate Section 467 (b) which limited the ICC/IP representation to only one (I) seat. It was mentioned that the NICP Regional Office Xl submitted to the NICP Commission En Banc their position on the proposed amendment to the IPMR Guidelines allowing selection of Provincial and City IPMR per legislative district subject to the concurrence of the LGU concerned. Based on the foregoing discussion, we respectfully submit a favorable recommendation on the idea of per legislative district. Should such change be adopted, let it be uniform among LGUs and subject to the existence of ICCs/lPs within the legislative district. Finally, since the Department will be anticipating the decision of the NICP En Banc on the matter as well as NICP's coordination to this Department on the matter, this is hereby rendered not as an officially numbered Department opinion, but as an initial position on the issue. Pending the issuance of an NICP En Banc resolution, the selection of ICCs/lPs is still subject to Section 12 of NCIP Administrative Order No. I s. 2019, NATIONAL GUIDELINES FOR THE MANDATORY REPRESENTATION OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES IN LOCAL LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL", which states that: "The selection of the particular ICCs/lP representative to the local legislative council shall be in accordance with the local guideline that concerned ICCs/IPs shall adopt and promulgate, which considers the cycles of traditional or local activities xxx." We hope to assisted you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MARLO L. Undersecr GAN ry for Local Government OUSLG/MLVLLLS-LRALLD/kbm Page 2 of 3
